clue.text: Sort of apron, if extended at the front

definitions.text: Sort of apron, if extended at the front

parts.words: Sort of apron, if extended at the front
parts.note: an apron that is pinned so that it covers the wearer's front; the old phrase 'pinned afore' is where the garment's name comes from

explanation.surface: A dressmaker's note on how a particular apron is made longer at the front.
explanation.walkthrough: The garment's name comes from 'pin afore': a bib that is pinned to the dress at the front, making an apron that covers the upper body.
explanation.definitionFit: This garment is a sleeveless apron-dress whose bib reaches up over the chest, an apron enlarged at the front.

clue.text: Say mistletoe needs trim as it is brought in

indicators.note: the words 'as it' are brought into the middle of another word

parts.note: to pare is to trim by cutting away the edge
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gardener's remark that mistletoe must be cut back when carried indoors at Christmas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is brought in' puts AS IT inside PARE. 'Say' marks mistletoe as an example of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Mistletoe lives on host trees and draws nourishment from them, an example of a parasite.

clue.text: Simpleton gravely so miscalled by mechanicals

definitions.meaning: in A Midsummer Night's Dream the rustic workmen, the 'mechanicals', keep calling Ninus's tomb by a garbled name

explanation.surface: A fool is clumsily mislabelled by a troupe of workmen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gravely' refers to a grave: Bottom and his fellow tradesmen meet at 'Ninny's tomb', mangling the name of Ninus.
explanation.definitionFit: A ninny is a foolish person, and also the mechanicals' mistake for Ninus at his tomb.

clue.text: Be raring to come across mischievous child in the family?

parts.note: to fall over something is to come across it by chance
one's means belonging to oneself, so within one's own family
an elf is a playful, impish little person

explanation.surface: A relative is keen to meet the household's naughty youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: The family's mischievous child is one's elf, which read together spells the final word of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To fall over oneself to do something is to be desperately eager, raring to do it.

clue.text: Animal English family put into pot

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep
kin means family or relatives

explanation.surface: Someone stuffs a creature and an English family into a cooking pot.
explanation.definitionFit: A ramekin is a small dish for baking and serving an individual portion, a kind of pot.

clue.text: Seconds to take eagerly at such a meal?

definitions.text: Seconds to take eagerly at such a meal?

parts.note: to lap up something is to take it in eagerly, like a cat with milk

explanation.surface: At a lavish feast, diners greedily go back for second helpings.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a whole the clue describes the meal; read in pieces it builds the word. 'Seconds' here are extra helpings in the surface, but give only S.
explanation.definitionFit: A slap-up meal is a lavish, generous British spread, exactly where people eagerly take second helpings.

clue.text: Play one may retrospectively find outrageous?

definitions.meaning: John Osborne's 1956 stage drama, a landmark of the 'angry young men'
taken literally, to view something with fury after the event

explanation.surface: A drama that, on reflection, one might consider scandalous.
explanation.walkthrough: The play is John Osborne's famous 1956 drama; the second reading takes the title literally as remembering with rage.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of Osborne's famous play, and literally describes recalling something furiously.

clue.text: Attaining power initially in minister's job

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word it follows

parts.note: to reach a goal is to attain it

explanation.surface: Gaining power early on is what a church minister's role is all about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes P from 'power', placed at the front of REACHING.
explanation.definitionFit: Preaching sermons is the central work of a minister of religion.

clue.text: Language buff

definitions.meaning: to buff is to rub to a shine

explanation.surface: A tongue that also means to rub something shiny.
explanation.definitionFit: Polish is the language of Poland, and to polish is to buff a surface until it shines.

clue.text: Dirt's taken to cave

parts.note: grot is British slang for dirt or rubbish

explanation.surface: Grime is carried into a cavern.
explanation.walkthrough: GROT is informal British for filth; the 's (has) and 'taken' just join it to TO.
explanation.definitionFit: A grotto is a small picturesque cave, natural or artificial.

clue.text: Put in proper name of an organ

indicators.note: the instruction tells us to put one piece inside another word

parts.note: proper in the sense of genuine, real

explanation.surface: An instruction to insert the correct name of an organ of the body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put in' tells us to place N inside REAL, giving RE-N-AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Renal is the adjective for things relating to the kidneys, a bodily organ.

clue.text: Mail for American during dinner that gets stony cold

indicators.note: one thing happening during another is placed inside it

parts.note: dinner is a meal
mail as in chain mail is armour, spelt the American way

explanation.surface: A letter arrives mid-dinner for an American guest, and the room turns frosty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mail' looks like post but is chain mail, and 'for American' asks for the US spelling without a U.
explanation.definitionFit: Marmoreal means like marble, so cold, white and hard as stone, the poetic sense here.

clue.text: TV channel receiving severe criticism, if prices did this?

parts.note: Sky is a British satellite television broadcaster
to get a rocket is British slang for a severe telling-off

explanation.surface: A broadcaster comes under fire for what happened to the cost of living.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receiving' only joins the channel to the criticism, which follows it rather than going inside. A rocket is British slang for a dressing-down.
explanation.definitionFit: Prices that skyrocket climb steeply and suddenly; the definition is the verb in its past-time slot, phrased as a question.

clue.text: Foreign cash used in part of the country

definitions.meaning: dollars, informally called ... in America, foreign currency to a British reader
Buckinghamshire, an English county just north-west of London, is often shortened to this

explanation.surface: Foreign money circulating in one region of the nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Bucks is slang for US dollars, and also the short form of Buckinghamshire, an English county.

clue.text: Time to lock up abbey that inspired Wordsworth

parts.note: to intern someone is to confine them, especially in wartime

explanation.surface: Closing time comes for the abbey that inspired a great poet.
explanation.walkthrough: Wordsworth wrote 'Lines Composed a Few Miles above Tintern Abbey', about a ruined abbey in the Wye valley in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Tintern Abbey is the ruined Welsh monastery celebrated in Wordsworth's famous poem.

clue.text: Architect very wrongly employed to start country home

parts.note: John Nash designed Regent Street and the Brighton Pavilion
ill means badly or wrongly, as in ill-treated

indicators.note: to start means take the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: An architect is badly misused when hired to begin building a house in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to start' takes E from 'employed'. 'Country' is country music, not the countryside: the Tennessee city is its home.
explanation.definitionFit: Nashville, Tennessee, is famous as the capital of country and western music.

clue.text: Tolkien monster did not reveal showy flower

parts.note: orcs are the brutish goblin-like creatures of Tolkien's Middle-earth
to have hidden something is to have not revealed it

explanation.surface: A fantasy creature keeps a striking bloom out of sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Orchids are flowers prized for their exotic, ornate and colourful blooms.

clue.text: Pastoral worker spends days extremely engrossed in Melville

indicators.note: something engrossed in a name is absorbed into the middle of it

parts.note: Herman Melville wrote Moby-Dick

indicators.note: extremely asks for the outermost letters of the word days

explanation.surface: A farmhand passes the time absorbed in reading Moby-Dick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' gives D and S, the first and last letters of 'days', and 'engrossed in' puts them inside HERMAN. 'spends' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A herdsman tends cattle or sheep, a worker on pasture land.

clue.text: Source of minerals found behind tree on land

parts.note: the ash is a common tree
ore is rock from which metals and minerals are extracted

explanation.surface: Prospectors find rich deposits behind a tree, safely away from the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Source of minerals' reads as the definition at first, but the definition is 'on land' at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashore means on or to the land as opposed to at sea.

clue.text: Prophet and priest taking up pilgrimage

parts.note: Eli is the priest who raised Samuel in the Old Testament

indicators.note: in a down entry, taking up means the word is read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: the hajj is the pilgrimage to Mecca, also spelt haj

explanation.surface: A holy man and a priest set off on a religious journey.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'taking up' makes the pilgrimage read from bottom to top. Eli was the priest who brought up Samuel.
explanation.definitionFit: Elijah is one of the great prophets of the Hebrew Bible.

clue.text: Unusual English beach? Yes and no

indicators.note: something unusual is out of the ordinary, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Is a pebbly English shore really a beach? Both answers seem true.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusual' rearranges the letters of ENGLISH. 'Yes and no' says the definition is only half right: this is a beach of pebbles, not the sandy kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Shingle is a mass of pebbles forming a beach, so it is a beach and also only the stones on one.

clue.text: Drink more in mess as commander

parts.note: to sup is to drink in sips

indicators.note: letters in a mess are jumbled up, so the word more is rearranged

explanation.surface: An officer has another drink in the mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in mess' rearranges MORE to REMO. The mess looks like the officers' dining room.
explanation.definitionFit: A supremo is a person in overall charge, a supreme commander.

clue.text: A tax credit at first for leisure-wear

indicators.note: the credit piece comes first, ahead of the others

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
VAT is value added tax, the British sales tax

explanation.surface: A sales tax on casual clothes, with a credit up front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For leisure-wear' reads as the purpose of a tax; this neckcloth is casual wear worn open-necked instead of a tie.
explanation.definitionFit: A cravat is a loose scarf-like neckcloth worn casually in place of a tie.

clue.text: Soundly criticise theatrical entertainment

indicators.note: here it means judged by how the word sounds when spoken

parts.note: to review a book or show is to criticise it

explanation.surface: A harsh critique of a variety show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soundly' looks like 'thoroughly' but means the word is judged by its sound: REVIEW and REVUE are said the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: A revue is a light stage show of sketches, songs and dances, a theatrical entertainment.

clue.text: Prosecuted trouble-maker with energy and caused pain

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous little devil
E is the physics symbol for energy
something that ached caused pain

explanation.surface: A mischief-maker, full of beans, was put on trial and suffered for it.
explanation.definitionFit: To impeach an official is to charge them formally with misconduct, a kind of prosecution.

clue.text: Eating very healthy share

indicators.note: a word eating another takes it inside itself

parts.note: hale means healthy, as in hale and hearty

explanation.surface: A very healthy person takes only their portion of the meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eating' puts V inside HALE.
explanation.definitionFit: To halve something is to share it equally between two.

clue.text: In electoral process, liberal has to confront sudden change of views

indicators.note: liberal sits inside the electoral process, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: voting is how an election is decided
L is the abbreviation for Liberal, as in the British party
to face someone is to confront them

explanation.surface: During an election a Liberal politician must face up to a dramatic U-turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has to' is only a link between the two halves; 'confront' supplies the second half of the French-derived phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A volte-face is a complete reversal of opinion or policy, an about-turn.

clue.text: Energy having left me returning — I'm supernaturally animated

parts.note: go means energy or vigour, as in 'full of go'

indicators.note: returning means the little word me is read backwards

explanation.surface: Out of steam and heading home, a speaker claims to be magically brought to life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' reverses the little word me. 'Left' looks like 'departed' but is just its abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A golem is a clay figure in Jewish folklore given life by magic, speaking here in the first person.

clue.text: Having removed shirt, start using iron

parts.note: a tee is a T-shirt
a garment that is off has been removed

explanation.surface: A golfer peels off a shirt before playing the first shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iron' looks like laundry but is a golf club; teeing off is starting a hole, often with an iron.
explanation.definitionFit: To tee off is to play the opening stroke of a golf hole, starting with a club such as an iron.

clue.text: The points Wilson made were half this number

definitions.text: The points Wilson made were half this number

parts.words: The points Wilson made were half this number
parts.note: President Woodrow Wilson set out his peace programme in a famous list of points in 1918; this clue is number 28, double that list

explanation.surface: A history question about how many points an American president made.
explanation.walkthrough: Woodrow Wilson's 1918 peace plan was his famous list of points; double that count and you reach 28, the clue's own number.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilson's peace programme had this many points, which is exactly half of twenty-eight, the clue's number.
